transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is now on his way to Asia.
His first stop will be the Philippines.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn has more from Seoul.
>> President Trump will attend a special summit of the U.S.
and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations,
or ASEAN, in Manila.
On the sidelines of ASEAN, Trump will also attend the first summit
in two years of the Quad grouping,
which also includes Japan, India, and Australia.
On his final stop in Shenzhen, China,
Trump is due to participate in a summit
of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation Organization,
or APEC.
He'll then hold an unprecedented meeting
with Russian President Vladimir Putin
and China's leader Xi Jinping.
Trump says he wants to discuss nuclear arms control
with his counterparts.
But China, which has the smallest nuclear arsenal
of the three powers, says the summit will be about promoting
world peace and stability.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
>> Just before he left the White House Monday morning,
President Trump said he might also meet
with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.
Trump said it will be up to Chinese leader Xi Jinping
if that meeting happens.
The Trump administration is taking new steps to prevent China
from gaining access to advanced U.S. computing chips
and servers.
The new rule announced by the Commerce Department Monday
seeks to close a loophole that allows China
to remotely access American AI technology.
Here's NPR Scott Horsley.
>> This new rule is designed to close that loophole
by requiring data centers in third countries
to police the people they're working for.
And if they're doing business with, say, China, for example,
they would be subject to additional restrictions.
The rule also limits chip sales to countries like Malaysia,
Indonesia, and Thailand, which are seen as at higher risk
of having those chips diverted to China.
>> The rules that govern the export of the U.S.'s
most powerful chips are in the spotlight
after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned
over links to a woman suspected of spying for China.
A gallon of diesel now costs less than $6.
NPR's Willa Rubin reports on the week's long decline
in prices for both diesel and gasoline.
>> Diesel is dropping because of another drop in crude prices.
Crude oil is the raw, goopy oil that comes out of the ground.
Refineries then turn that into diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel.
Crude is getting cheaper because more oil is getting
out of the Middle East, so supply and demand.
More supply here means lower prices for oil
and related products.
And here's why lower diesel prices matters.
Diesel is the workhorse of the economy.
Much of the nation's farming and trucking runs on diesel.
When diesel goes up over time, so does the price
of just about everything.
So this is a counterweight to inflation.
But a gallon of diesel still costs more than $2
more than a year ago.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
>> This is "NPR News."
What of Mexico's most notorious drug lords has died?
NPR's Zeta Peralta reports he'd been in prison
for nearly 40 years.
>> He was widely known as El Jefe de Jefes,
the boss of bosses.
That's because in the '70s and '80s Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo
helped wrangle disparate and warring drug cartels
into one centrally-run organization
that he called the Federation.
That eventually led to Mexican cartels becoming some
of the biggest drug-running organizations in the world.
Gallardo was convicted of murdering DEA agent Kiki Camarena
and has been in jail since 1989.
The U.S. sought his extradition, but he was widely believed
to hold secrets about some of the most powerful figures
in Mexico.
And now he has died without ever revealing the secrets.
According to Jalisco state authorities,
Gallardo succumbed to organ failure.
He was 80 years old.
Ada Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
>> The murder case against Lindsay Clancy will go to trial
for a second time.
A Massachusetts judge Monday set Clancy's retrial
on the killing of her three young children for late March.
Clancy's first trial ended with a hung jury.
Her case has raised issues about maternal mental health.
The defenses argue that Clancy was suffering
from postpartum psychosis.
Tech shares leading global markets lower,
the major markets in Asia declining
following Monday's losses on Wall Street.
Invidia stocks helped drag the U.S. market lower
following last week's resignation of CEO Jensen Huang.
FAA contractor L3 Harris Technologies also fell
after Trump administration officials suggested
that it may be at fault for Friday's nationwide ground stop.

topics.text: Trump departs for Asia, starting with a Manila summit of ASEAN and the Quad
Trump says he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, depending on China's Xi
Commerce Department issues new rule closing loophole for China to access US AI chips remotely
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns over links to woman suspected of spying for China
Diesel prices fall below $6 a gallon as crude oil declines amid Middle East supply
Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, Mexico's notorious drug lord known as El Jefe de Jefes, dies at 80
Massachusetts judge sets March retrial for Lindsay Clancy in killing of her three children
Tech shares, led by Nvidia, drag global markets lower after Wall Street losses
FAA contractor L3 Harris Technologies falls after administration suggests it caused nationwide ground stop
